deviations.reason: The planner prices every bundle for the runner class its profile names. The blacksmith and hybrid profiles price Blacksmith 4 to 32 vCPU machines; the github profile prices GitHub's public ubuntu-24.04, 4 vCPU and 16 GiB. An oc-8cpu-32gb ARC pod is at least that size, so github prices are an upper bound on our pods, not an optimistic guess; the rented hosted lane (2 vCPU for a private repository) is charged the router's hosted slowdown. The blacksmith profile also refuses this target at the main-validation cap (86 jobs planned for 77).

Upstream's automatic tiers run these runtime-integration files only when the test itself changes, and its Full Release Validation runs them all. Mode-B is the fork's one broad acceptance run and has always run them. Dropping them would buy speed by testing less.

deviations.mode_b: 130 (upstream's pull-request tier) minus the worker-e2e rows
deviations.reason: Upstream's 77-row main tier protects its shared runner pool from hourly main. Mode-B runs the bundles on its own runners (hosted bundles packed into jobs, each self-hosted bundle in a job of its own), so the planner's row cap only has to admit the plan, and the pinned compact contract binds the job count that results. With the release-only runtime files kept, the main-tier cap refuses this target (88 bundles planned for 77). 130 is the limit upstream gives the same compactMode in its pull-request tier. The worker-e2e rows are subtracted exactly as upstream does, though Mode-B does not run them.

exclusions.upstream: includeReleaseOnlyPluginShards: false in every ci.yml tier; plugin-prerelease.yml runs agentic-plugins hourly instead
exclusions.mode_b: kept: each runs whole on its own routed row, as before

exclusions.upstream: includeReleaseOnlyRuntimeTests: false in the automatic tiers; Full Release Validation runs them
